core_obligations: Derive exactness of p_* on modules and surjectivity in (2) from the abelian-sheaves version of the statement (proof lines 7299-7303).
Use p^{-1}O = O_p to conclude p^{-1} = p^* and identify p^{-1}p_*M -> M with the adjunction counit for modules, which is O_p-linear (proof lines 7304-7308).

For (3), exhibit the topos of G-sets with the forgetful point, identify p^{-1} with forgetting the action and p_* with Map(G, -), display the maps M -> Map(G, M) -> M occurring in the direct sum decomposition, and show that they are not O_p-linear in general (proof lines 7309-7336).
proof_roadmap: Reduce exactness and surjectivity to the abelian-sheaves case.
Identify the map with the adjunction counit to get linearity.
Produce the G-sets counterexample for the non-linearity statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves three facts about the pushforward along a point p of a ringed topos: exactness of p_* on modules, linearity of the canonical surjection p^{-1}p_*M -> M, and the failure in general of linearity for the functorial direct sum decomposition known for abelian sheaves. Parts (1) and the surjectivity in (2) are reduced to the abelian-sheaves version of the same statement, and linearity of the counit follows from the identification p^{-1}O = O_p, which makes p^{-1} = p^* so that the map in question is the adjunction counit for modules (proof lines 7298-7308). Part (3) is proved by an explicit counterexample: for a group G one considers the topos of G-sets with its point to Sets, where p^{-1} forgets the action and p_* is the right adjoint Map(G, -), and the maps in the direct sum decomposition are displayed and shown not to be O_p-linear (proof lines 7309-7336). H2: the reduction for parts (1) and (2) and the explicit counterexample for part (3) are the substance.
